claim: Larger model scale is associated with lower measured depth of unlearning erasure, attributed to greater model capacity causing less representational shift from training data differences.
falsifier: On a family of models of different sizes, apply the same unlearning method and compute the activation-patching-based depth score; verify that the score decreases with scale.

conditions: unlearning methods applied to models of varying scale
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported models and unlearning configurations; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Increase in model scale–measured depth of erasure principle

claim: Successful model formulations that become canonical instantiations of a theory increase the theory's applicability to a wider range of problems and provide more precise solutions, and over time theories become more rigorous through the development of such canonical models.
falsifier: One can test this by tracking the historical development of a theory, identifying when model formulations become canonical, and measuring changes in the range of problems addressed and the precision of solutions.

conditions: Over time, as specific successful model formulations become closely associated with the theory
exclusions: Limited to the reviewed literature on theory development in neuroscience and cognitive science; transferability to other scientific fields is unestablished.

title: Development of canonical model–applicability to a wider principle
